sections.heading: Highway transportation system
sections.markdown:
# Highway transportation system

FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A01
The Highway Transportation System is the connected network of roads, streets and highways used by public and private traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A01
The transportation system aims to move people and goods safely, efficiently and promptly while protecting the environment. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A01
Every road user shares responsibility for following the system’s rules and cooperating with others. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A01
The road network supports ordinary trips, deliveries and emergency responses. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A01
The system’s people component includes drivers, passengers, pedestrians, road workers, police, emergency personnel and children at play. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A01
Vehicles sharing the system range from passenger cars and bicycles to buses, trucks, farm vehicles and emergency vehicles. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A02
The roads component includes Interstate, United States, state and county routes, along with toll roads and parkways. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A02
The transportation network makes personal travel, work, school, shopping and recreation possible. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A02
Vehicle manufacturing, highway construction, freight movement, travel and vehicle repair are economic activities supported by the road system. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A02
OMV manages licensing and vehicle-related matters such as plates, registration, fees and titles. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A02
Police, highway patrol and sheriff’s departments contribute to safe travel through enforcement. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A02
Traffic courts support enforcement of traffic law. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A02
Highway engineering improves the road system, while vehicle engineering improves vehicle safety and operation. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A02
Emergency responders and trauma centers work to reduce collision losses during the emergency and afterward. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A02
Public education prepares road users through knowledge of traffic rules, vehicle-operation skills and attitudes consistent with safety. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A02
Collisions can impose personal losses as well as financial costs for wages, medical care, rehabilitation, services and property damage. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A03
Traffic-safety comparisons can use collision and death counts relative to the distance traveled. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A03
The guide’s dated Louisiana fatality-cause list identifies alcohol, distraction, aggressive behavior and missing seat-belt use. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A03
Drivers, pedestrians and bicyclists may have different needs and viewpoints when they share the transportation system. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A03
A driver needs to anticipate mistakes and unsafe actions by other road users. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A03
Different vehicle types have different steering, braking, speed-control and performance capabilities. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A03
A vehicle’s equipment, age, condition and maintenance affect its handling. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A03
Understanding the capabilities of trucks or motorcycles matters even to a driver who never operates those vehicles. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A03
Unsafe speeds create hazards, particularly on freeways and expressways. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A04
Driving below the posted limit can still be too fast for the weather, traffic or the driver’s physical condition. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A04
Highway design takes expected traffic volume and vehicle mix into account when choosing lanes, shoulders and medians. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A04
A parish road is maintained and regulated by its parish. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F28 | anchor: A04
A state highway is regulated by the state. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F29 | anchor: A04
The guide describes United States highways as a route system that predates the Interstate program. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F30 | anchor: A04
Interstate highways carry large traffic volumes on routes across the country. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]
